subject: history
title: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia

segments.say: Philippines, 1946: pressure crosses the line. Nationalist pressure rises past the threshold after the Second World War, the United States grants independence, and the control bar falls. Point at the transmission arrow leaving the scene on your student notes before it lands next door.
questions: What crosses the threshold in this scene, and what follows?
Where does the transmission arrow carry the example?

segments.say: Indonesia, 1949: the example raises pressure. Indonesian nationalists point to a neighbour that has already won, pressure rises in their own campaign, and the Netherlands recognises Indonesian independence in 1949. Now try the recognition-year questions on your worksheet.
questions: What did Indonesian campaigners gain from the Philippine win?
In which year was Indonesian independence recognised?

segments.say: Malaya, 1957: pressure rises, control falls. Two neighbours are now independent, so the Malayan campaign starts from a stronger position; the pressure bar rises while the British control bar keeps falling, and Malaya wins independence in 1957. Check the order of the stages against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Why does the Malayan campaign start from a stronger position?
Which bar rises and which bar falls in this scene?

segments.say: Singapore, 1959: the chain reaches home. Campaigners have watched three neighbours win in thirteen years, and Singapore wins internal self-government in 1959. Keep the whole chain - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959 - in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What exactly did Singapore win in 1959?
What is the whole decolonisation chain, in order?
segments.watchFor: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home. Listen for students who treat the four territories as four separate stories with no connection. Send them back to the transmission arrows: The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959.
